SOURCINGRECORD / Nonbinding redline

Keep the conversation inside its envelope.

Bids Signal is a proposed module for supplier-consented negotiation on approved non-price terms. Its working object is a nonbinding draft with a policy envelope, redline and human approval checkpoint.

DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA

A conversation
with boundaries.

SOURCE · COMPARISON · REVIEW

THE JOB / THE BASIS

Which non-price terms could you safely review in a supervised pilot?

For indirect procurement heads and category managers at midmarket companies with repeat tail-spend purchases.

INPUT

A comparable quote, explicit supplier consent and an authorized envelope.

OUTPUT / PROPOSED

A source-linked nonbinding counteroffer and inspectable offer history.

THE WORKFLOW

A specific job.
A visible review point.

Each step retains the source and the unresolved exception.

01

Set the boundaries

Freeze price, quantity, specification, payment and liability terms. Authorize only the stated delivery range.

02

Confirm participation

The supplier can decline or withdraw. Consent is specific to the permitted discussion.

03

Review the draft

The manager reviews the redline before any binding term or external action.

THE EXAMPLE

A draft inside
15–30 days.

Juniper’s price and specification stay fixed. Delivery is the permitted discussion. A 45-day proposal and any consent bypass are blocked.

LIMITS / INTEGRATION SCOPE

Controls that stay in view.

A proposed module is a bounded workflow, not a general-purpose autonomous agent. Source-to-pay mapping would be assessed within a permissioned pilot; no production integration is claimed.

  • The RF-202 envelope allows delivery of 15–30 days.
  • A 45-day proposal is blocked.
  • Consent and prohibited concessions cannot be overridden.
Read all controls

FAQ

Before you choose the module.

Does human review make every override permissible?

No. A reviewer may correct extraction or choose a permitted alternative, but cannot bypass consent or prohibited concessions.

Can I send the draft from the demo?

No. Send, acceptance and binding action are disabled. Simulated approval stays inside the fictional example.
